newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up at a five-week high vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up at a five-week high vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed at a five-week high of 8.2977 against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2985 on strong sentiment, traders said.
Dealers said more dollar selling due to the growth of China's trade surplus and increasing demand for yuan before the year-end encouraged pro-yuan sentiment.
The yuan opened slightly up at an intra-day low of 8.2983 and consolidated up steadily for most of the session, hitting an intra-day high of 8.2973.
Trading was dull, with most done at 8.2980, traders said.
"There was strong buying for the yuan between 8.2990 and 8.3000, which stopped the fall going too deep," one dealer said.
"With the year-end approaching, most China's banks need more local cash rather than dollars," he added.
"But the upward trend will be capped by the central bank in the short term," a second dealer said. "The People's Bank of China will not allow the yuan to fluctuate sharply."
Dealers expect the yuan to fall slightly on Thursday.
The yuan closed up at 7.3000 from 7.3070 against 100 Japanese yen and down at 1.0727 from 1.0706 against the Hong Kong dollar.
